item.title: Texas RB Hollywood Smothers ruled out against Ole Miss
item.description: DALLAS, TX - OCTOBER 10: Texas Longhorns running back Hollywood Smothers (2) runs up field during the Allstate Red River Rivalry between the Texas Longhorns and Oklahoma Sooners on October 10, 2026, at Cotton Bowl Stadium in Dallas, TX. (Photo by Brian Rothmuller/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Texas Longhorns senior running back Hollywood Smothers will not be available for Saturday’s game against the Ole Miss Rebels in Austin after he was ruled out on Friday’s SEC-mandated injury report. The 5’11, 196-pounder was downgraded from doubtful on Thursday after missing practice earlier in the week with a shoulder injury. Smothers also sat out against Tennessee in the SEC opener with a lower-leg injury. Already ruled out were junior edge Colin Simmons, and freshman edge Richard Wesley as sophomore wide receiver Kaliq Lockett and senior offensive lineman Jaydon Chatman were also downgraded from doubtful to out on Friday. Freshman running back Derrek Cooper remained probable while sophomore offensive lineman Jackson Christian is questionable in his addition to the injury report. Cooper did not play against Florida last weekend — Texas head coach Steve Sarkisian said that he was not at 100 percent. Cooper previously suffered an ankle injury in the season opener that kept him out the following week against Ohio State.

item.title: Xavier wraps up exhibition play at 3-0. Why it matters.
item.description: The wins won't show up in the standings, nor will they improve Xavier's NCAA Tournament resume or count toward its record when the regular season begins. But Xavier's 3-0 record in October exhibitions after a 76-70 win over Kent State Oct. 23 at Cintas Center is something worth carrying into the regular season. The Musketeers notched three wins that tested different parts of a transfer portal-fueled team still in the early stages of gelling. Outside against Dayton earlier this month, Xavier built a sizeable lead before holding off a Flyers' comeback that trimmed the margin to as little as one point. The Musketeers followed with an 86-70 road victory over Tennessee, rallying from an eight-point halftime deficit in Knoxville against a program that has reached three consecutive Elite Eights and was picked No. 8 in the AP's preseason Top 25 poll. On Friday, Xavier's final preseason tune-up offered a different test when Rob Senderoff's Golden Flashes visited Cintas Center. Xavier didn't handle its business in a way a Big East school should against a mid-major program, but it was a far cry from one year ago, when an exhibition home loss to Murray State felt synonymous with a "Danger Alert" ahead of a 15-18 season and last-place finish in the Big East. Three games, three different game scripts and paths to victory. For a team with several newcomers, that variety could prove valuable long after the exhibition games are forgotten. College basketball rosters across the country have become increasingly transient, and Xavier is no exception. Integrating new players involves more than figuring out who can score, rebound or defend. It requires building chemistry, establishing roles and learning how to respond when the momentum is not on your side or you're in a hostile road environment. Second-year head coach Richard Pitino has touted the depth of this Xavier roster, and the exhibition schedule has offered an early opportunity to see how that depth translates to the court. Furthermore, that depth has been tested with freshmen Kalek House and Asher Elson missing multiple games. Of course, three exhibition games cannot establish how deep a team truly is or guarantee that its pieces will fit when the stakes rise next month. But that trio of contests offered valuable repetitions, particularly for players adjusting to new teammates, a new system or a larger role. While these victories won't count, the lessons do. Xavier got 120 study minutes against three different opponents for the real test on Monday, Nov. 2, when Xavier hosts Mount St. Mary's in a game that will count. item.title: Brewers fans bought more National League Champions gear than any team in history
item.description: Milwaukee Brewers cashed in on World Series hype like no other team in history. According to MLB store data, Brewers merch hit an all-time record for sales in the two days after the team swept the National League Championship Series. More Brewers merch was sold in those 48 hours than any other pennant winner on record, MLB communications manager Claire Skelley said. Exclusive: Order NL Championship Book The previous 48-hour record was set by the Philadelphia Phillies in 2022. Brewers fans moved about 5% more in sales than Phillies fans did. Sales also outsold the Chicago Cubs' NLCS drop by 14%, the 2024 Dodgers by 60% and the 2025 Dodgers by double. The hottest item was the NLCS Locker Room-style shirts. Brewers fans set an all-time record for raw NLCS Locker Room shirt sales, according to MLB store data. item.description: Photo Credit: USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Connect | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Michael Joseph Sugue, Manager On this week’s WWE SmackDown in Ontario, California . Things got extremely heated between Cody Rhodes and Randy Orton. Now, WWE Crown Jewel 2026 will be the site of the rematch, the rubber bout that finally settles all the bad blood between these two over the past year. However, it won’t just be a normal match- how can it be? The “American Nightmare” laid down the law, and the “Apex Predator” agreed. Cody Rhodes and Randy Orton Finish It at WWE Crown Jewel 2026 Rhodes did the unthinkable on last week’s SmackDown after punt-kicking Baron Corbin flush in the head . The WWE Universe was shocked, and for a split second, even his former mentor and arch-rival Orton couldn’t believe his eyes. Friday night this week, Orton would come out to address the elephant in the room. What was that? Well, Randy claimed that Cody couldn’t do it, but he did it; he pulled the trigger. The “Viper” made it known that he was proud of Rhodes for doing what he did. That said, he knows, and everyone knows, that Cody will “hesitate” when it counts the most: against him. When the opportunity presents itself again, Cody will fall short, and he’s going to be back to square one. Photo Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Cody Rhodes would come out and voice his opinion. Rhodes made it known that he was well aware of how dangerous Randy is. He punted Triple H, Shawn Michaels, and even Cody’s father, the late, great “American Dream” Dusty Rhodes. However, every time Orton made a statement, he wouldn’t follow through, as Cody pushed the narrative that Orton is a self-sabotaging screw-up. Photo Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Things got extremely heated as WWE officials surrounded the ring. SmackDown General Manager Nick Aldis tried to break up the impending fight and announced that if they wanted to do it, it wouldn’t be tonight. However, it will happen as he sanctions a match at WWE Crown Jewel 2026 . Rhodes would remark that this next bout isn’t going to be a normal match. He wants to end it, and he wants it to be a Last Man Standing Match. Orton would agree, setting the stage for the final showdown between Randy Orton and Cody Rhodes. item.title: A Glove-First Outfielder
item.description: San Diego, CA - September 27: Jase Bowen #4 of the San Diego Padres catches a fly ball hit by Jordan Lawlar #10 of the Arizona Diamondbacks at Petco Park on September 27, 2026 in San Diego, CA. (Photo by K.C. Alfred / The San Diego Union-Tribune via Getty Images) Welcome to our series grading every member of the San Diego Padres’ 40-man roster. The roster being evaluated is current as of Oct. 18, prior to the end of the World Series. Because of that, it will include players who will be free agents once the postseason concludes. Each player will be graded on their performance in the 2026 season, including the playoffs. That performance will be weighted based on how much time the player spent with the team (availability is the best ability). A Glove-First Outfielder After being drafted by the Pittsburgh Pirates in the 11th round of the 2019 draft, Jase Bowen flashed potential in his final season in the Pirates’ system. In 2025, he slashed .272/.353/.449 across four levels of the minor leagues. Most impressively, Bowen hit .294 with an .870 OPS in 36 games for Triple-A Indianapolis. In November of ‘25, Bowen elected free agency and signed with San Diego. He posted a .292/.362/.600 slash line in 49 games with Triple-A El Paso before being called up to make his MLB debut. Overall Grade: C- To that end, Bowen struggled. He never quite found a groove at the plate in the big leagues. Bowen often looked overwhelmed against big-league pitching, batting an anemic .146 with a .438 OPS. The power all but disappeared. Bowen had hit 13 homers in 49 games with El Paso, but launched just two in 83 contests at the big-league level. Some of that is due to his usage as a defensive replacement. Bowen was really only put in games late, often not starting. Of the 83 games that Bowen played in, he started in less than a quarter of them. He boasts a phenomenal glove, posting +2 Fielding Run Value and +1 Outs Above Average in such a small sample (283.0 INN). Still, his glove is not enough to keep him on the roster. Bowen has a potent bat, but he needs more time to develop. Starting the season in Triple-A to get more time against high-caliber pitching could help him mature enough to face big-leaguers. Alternatively, if he shows improvement during Cactus League play, Bowen could work his way onto the Opening Day roster. That said, Bowen needs to improve, otherwise he’s not going to last long on this squad in a stacked outfield crop.

item.title: Lexington rallies behind hometown star Sal Frelick as Brewers begin World Series campaign
item.description: A hometown kid is taking baseball’s biggest stage, and Lexington is rallying behind him. Sal Frelick, a Lexington High School and Boston College standout who now plays right field for the Milwaukee Brewers, made his World Series debut Friday night. Fans gathered at Craft Food Halls in Lexington for Game 1, where custom shirts featuring Frelick’s No. 10 were handed out as the crowd prepared to watch the hometown star. “No matter what the outcome is, he’s going to make everyone proud,” Matt Leppen of Craft Food Halls said. Frelick, 26, was a three-sport star at Lexington High before graduating in 2018 and continuing his career at Boston College. The Brewers selected him 15th overall in the 2021 draft. Two years later, he reached the majors and has since become a Gold Glove-winning right fielder for Milwaukee. “It’s something that every kid dreams from the time they step on the field from preball and Little League, and you’re like, ‘I want go to the World Series,’ and he’s doing it,” former Lexington Select Board member Suzie Barry said. Support for Frelick can be seen across town. Worthen Road was renamed Sal Frelick Way for the week, and the gazebo at Hastings Park, near Lexington High School, was lit in Brewers blue and gold. Barry, who has worked closely with Frelick and his family over the past couple years, said Frelick makes a significant donation to youth athletics in Lexington every year. “He’s never lost sight of where he came from,” Barry said. “I mean, he is just so dedicated, and he is a great all-around person and athlete.” Barry added, “He’s quiet. There’s no ego about him.” Cleve Coats, a former Massachusetts State Police trooper, said Frelick made an impression during his football days at Lexington High. “He was a senior captain and would always make time to stop to talk to little kids,” Coats said. “I’m with the police detail there; he would always come over and shake our hands on the ropeline.” For Lexington fans, Frelick’s World Series run is giving the town a reason to embrace October baseball, even if it isn’t the Red Sox. Asked whether a fan could bring themselves to wear Brewers gear, one person joked, “It’s a National League team, so it’s the best thing.” Leppen compared the atmosphere around Frelick’s run to the energy of the FIFA World Cup but said this one hits closer to home. “It matters to the local community because it’s so much more close to us,” Leppen said. “You know, Sal Frelick is a legend, so to have him on a big screen and be together and cheer him on, it’s a blessing.” The Brewers are trying to win their first World Series and have not reached the Fall Classic since 1982. Kentucky will have one more chance to tune up via an exhibition contest versus UCF on Oct. 28 at 6:00 PM ET. The game will be broadcast on the SEC Network. Here are five things to know for Kentucky’s fun exhibition win over the Red Raiders. Cats look crisp during 15-0 first-half run After the air was seemingly being sucked out of Rupp Arena, the Wildcats flipped the script, going on a 15-0 run over a three-minute stretch late in the first half. The impressive stretch on both ends of the floor gave the BBN a glimpse of what this team can produce right now. The run was highlighted by an emphatic Ousmane N’Diaye fast-break slam and a swaggy corner three from Milan Momcilovic. It was just what the doctor ordered for a late-arriving crowd inside Rupp Arena. Fans got a taste of how well this team can execute offensively and defensively when things are clicking. The 15-0 rally gave Kentucky a 37-33 halftime lead, despite Texas Tech controlling most of the first half. Taking care of the ball: After a rough start to exhibition play a week ago against Little Rock, the Cats came out careless with the ball again. Only this time, their opponent had the firepower to make them pay for it. With nine minutes remaining in the first half UK had already committed seven turnovers compared to just one for the Red Raiders. Texas Tech converted those turnovers into nine points on the other end. Thankfully, an explosive streak on offense erased the damage and then some. Half number two wasn’t exactly poetic basketball, but Kentucky tightened up the offense enough to beat a very good team on their home floor. UK would finish the game with only 11 total turnovers. Milan Momcilovic is proving to be worth every penny After looking sharp in UK’s first exhibition game against Little Rock, Milan Momcilovic would follow up his 4/7 shooting performance from deep by knocking down another pair of triples while scoring 15 points on only five shots. It’s evident through just two exhibition games that Momcilovic will be the straw that stirs the drink. When things get shaky for the Cats offensively, getting him the ball usually results in a solid possession, whether it’s facilitating a clean look for himself or a teammate. As long as he stays healthy, Momcilovic is going to have a season for the Kentucky record books. Alex Wilkins comes up big late After just two points in the first half, Wilkins remained confident and drilled several big late threes, including one from the logo. Those shots were not only critical plays in the game, but also important confidence builders for Wilkins heading into the regular season. At the end of the day, the roster Mark Pope has assembled in his third year will be heavily dependent on making jump shots. Last week against Little Rock, seven different Cats made a three-pointer, resulting in a collective 12/28 shooting performance behind the arc. Tonight against a much better defensive opponent, Kentucky made just 7/24 from deep, but Wilkins drilled the two that mattered most. He’d finish with 13 points on 3/9 shooting. Mason Williams balls out It’s not too late to buy Mason Williams stock if you’re late to buy in. The first year, Wildcat did a little bit of everything on Friday night and looked good doing it. His tenacious spirit and knack for putting the ball in the basket are starting to shine through. Tonight, Williams scored a casual 14 points, shooting 5/8 from the field. There’s now no denying that Mason Williams has carved out a role on this team, and now it’s just a matter of how big that role will be. The fans are clearly behind him, as reflected on social media after the big win. Now, let’s celebrate. Go CATS!

item.title: Bills Trade Pitch Lands $51.3 Million Tackling Machine From Rival
item.description: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 26: Jordyn Brooks #20 of the Miami Dolphins celebrates after a sack against the Atlanta Falcons during the second quarter in the game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 26, 2025 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) Getty The Buffalo Bills sure seem to need a shot of adrenaline on defense, despite their 5-1 record and the fact that true Super Bowl contenders usually don’t make big-time trades before the deadline. The Athletic’s Daniel Popper proposed a trade that would bring that adrenaline — and then some — with Miami Dolphins All-Pro linebacker Jordyn Brooks. Brooks has led the NFL in solo tackles twice—in 2021 and 2025—and earned NFL All-Pro honors for the first time in 2025, when he led the league with 183 combined tackles. The Dolphins signed him to a 3-year, $51.3 million contract extension on July 21. “The Dolphins are executing their tank effectively,” Popper wrote on October 22. “They have remained moderately competitive while still losing five straight games to begin the season. Their rookie class looks promising. The next step would be accruing some more draft capital for 2027. One issue, though, is they do not have many tradable players. Brooks, a reliable veteran off-ball linebacker, is one of the few. He signed a three-year extension in July and has close to $13 million in guaranteed salary in 2027, so any acquiring team would be making a multi-year commitment. The Dolphins would take on $15.6 million in dead money in 2027 if they traded Brooks. This regime, with coach Jeff Hafley and GM Jon-Eric Sullivan, has not been afraid of dead money thus far.” This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Bills Trade Pitch Lands $51.3 Million Tackling Machine From Rival appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: ‘He Went on the Flight, Huh? That’s Crazy’ — Chiefs Star Kenneth Walker III Makes Feelings Clear on Jalen Hurts’ Blood Clots After Same Diagnosis in HS
item.description: Jalen Hurts and Kenneth Walker III Kenneth Walker III’s message to Jalen Hurts came from his own experience. The Kansas City Chiefs running back, who dealt with blood clots in high school before winning Super Bowl MVP with the Seattle Seahawks last February, urged the Philadelphia Eagles QB to “stay positive” after the recent setback. Walker spoke days after the Eagles announced on Oct. 19 that Hurts’ blood clots had reached his lungs. He also reacted to Hurts flying back from London after the clot was diagnosed, a decision that has raised questions about how Philadelphia handled their QB’s health issue. Kenneth Walker III Gets Honest on Jalen Hurts’ Blood Clots’ Diagnosis When asked about Hurts, Walker pointed to his own past. “You know, obviously, I guess you know about what happened in high school, like with the blood clots and everything,” he said. “But he went on the flight, huh? That’s crazy.” Notably, Walker’s advice went beyond staying upbeat. He said Hurts should “do all the things necessary that he needs to do to get his body back right,” adding, “But yeah, I’ll be praying for him because that’s not something we should take lightly.” Hurts’ diagnosis is expected to keep him out for the rest of the 2026 season. Doctors at the Cleveland Clinic in London found a superficial clot in Hurts’ calf on Oct. 10, the day before the Eagles’ Week 5 game against the Jacksonville Jaguars. He was cleared to play and went 21-of-40 for 220 yards, with a 62-yard touchdown to Darius Cooper, in a 19-17 loss. Then he flew back to the U.S. with the team. The Eagles QB’s condition got worse in stages after he got home. A follow-up exam in Philadelphia on Oct. 14 showed the clot had moved, so the Eagles ruled him out of Week 6 and placed him on injured reserve. SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer Philadelphia lost 25-14 to the Carolina Panthers without him. A joint statement from the team and Hurts’ agent, Nicole Lynn, then revealed the new diagnosis of deep vein thrombosis, with clots in both lungs. Hurts is being treated with blood thinners, and a full recovery is expected. The Athletic reported that the NFL will not punish the Eagles because the league concluded the process that cleared Hurts to play in London was handled appropriately. In a statement Tuesday, the NFL also said it “had been in contact throughout the process with the Eagles medical personnel, and the Cleveland Clinic in London where the tests were conducted.” However, the NFL Players Association pushed back that night: “Before conclusions are drawn about how this situation was handled, there must be a full investigation into what occurred.” NFL commissioner Roger Goodell answered the union’s request Wednesday: “We welcome that.” The Eagles (2-4) host the Dallas Cowboys on Monday night at Lincoln Financial Field, their second straight game without Hurts. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: Yankees Must Pay 32-Year-Old Lefty $31.5 Million Next Season
item.description: The Yankees face a $31.5 million salary obligation to a 32-year-old left-handed pitcher next season, a substantial commitment with implications for their payroll. Getty Max Fried of the New York Yankees . Getty The World Series is set to start Friday night, and the New York Yankees for the 16th time in the last 17 years are not in it. It was 16 days ago that the Yankees were ousted from the postseason, swept in three games by the Tampa Bay Rays in the American League Division Series. In the final game, that sealed the Yankees’ fate for another season, starting pitcher Max Fried was one of the reasons the Bronx Bombers lost and went home. Fried lasted 5 2/3 innings and gave up four runs on seven hits including two home runs, but those four runs were one too many as the Yankees fell to the Rays 4-3. As they look toward 2027, the Yankees still owe Max Fried $174 million. That’s the total remaining on his contract which extends through the 2032 season, according to Spotrac‘s contract breakdown. None of Fried’s Yankees salary is deferred. After an injury-marred season, Fried’s payroll tab jumps from $14.5 million to $31.5 million in 2027, according to Spotrac . Fried signed the eight-year, $218 million contract in December 2024, a record for a left-hander that topped David Price’s seven-year deal with the Boston Red Sox by $1 million, according to The Associated Press . Half of the $20 million signing bonus arrived on Jan. 31, 2025, and the other half on Jan. 31, 2026, according to The Associated Press reporting . Spotrac lists the full $218 million as guaranteed. “No deferrals. No opt-outs,” wrote USA Today ‘s Bob Nightengale . New York Yankees’ Max Fried Contract Money Owed by Year Getty Max Fried of the New York Yankees. Fried collected $22 million in cash payments in each of 2025 and 2026 (a $12 million salary plus a $10 million bonus installment), which puts the Yankees’ actual outlay at $44 million so far, according to Spotrac . The remaining $174 million comes due at $29 million a year from 2027 through 2032. The balance falls to $145 million after 2027, $116 million after 2028, $87 million after 2029, $58 million after 2030 and $29 million after 2031. For luxury tax purposes, the deal counts at $27.25 million a year. The payroll charge rises to $31.5 million in 2027 because the $29 million salary replaces the $12 million one, while the bonus stays prorated at $2.5 million annually. Spotrac also lists a full no-trade clause. item.title: Mavericks ran smear campaign to justify Luka Doncic trade with Lakers: report
item.description: The Mavericks shocked the league by trading franchise star Luka Doncic to the Lakers in February 2025. Dallas reportedly ran a smear campaign to justify the shocking blockbuster deal, according to The Athletic’s Sam Amick. Reports about Doncic’s weight, work ethic and other slanders surfaced about the superstar upon his arrival to Los Angeles. Luka Doncic of the Los Angeles Lakers looks on during the game against the Golden State Warriors on October 21, 2026 at Crypto.Com Arena. Doncic has worked incredibly hard to negate any of the speculation surrounding his tenure in Dallas, including his weight. He has transformed his body, sporting the cover of Men’s Health with a new-and-improved form. This season, Doncic has a lot to prove to Lakers fans and to the rest of the league. Luka Doncic of the Los Angeles Lakers prepares to shoot a free throw during the game against the Golden State Warriors on October 21, 2026 at Crypto.Com Arena. NBAE via Getty Images Former Dallas Mavericks general manager Nico Harrison looks on before the game against the Oklahoma City Thunder at Dickie’s Arena. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect NBA general managers voted anonymously in a survey predicting the league’s Most Valuable Player. Doncic received zero votes for the prestigious award , a sign that while he is extremely talented his greatness has recently been overlooked by many. If Doncic can continue competing how he did on Opening Night against the Warriors, the Lakers have a chance of emerging as a top contender in a loaded Western Conference. The Lakers superstar has made his intentions extremely clear , penning a heartfelt letter to the city of LA ahead of the season opener.

item.description: Cooper Flagg injury update: Mavericks star exits after hard Pacers foul leads to skirmish originally appeared on The Sporting News . The Mavericks got off to a much better start Friday night than they did in their season opener, but an injury that sent Cooper Flagg threatens to put a damper on those good feelings. Flagg was on the receiving end of a Flagrant 1 foul from Indiana's Aaron Nesmith and remained down in pain under the basket before heading back to the locker room late in the first half. Double technicals were given to Nesmith and Naji Marshall after the play. https://t.co/P0xLooKo9S — ESPN (@espn) October 24, 2026 Flagg's Mavericks teammates quickly got in Nesmith's face, sparking a scuffle on the baseline as Dallas' second-year star remained down. Flagg also dealt with a left shoulder injury as a rookie, so the Mavericks could simply be opting for caution with a large lead over the Pacers. Flagg had 14 points, five rebounds and six assists in just 17 minutes on Friday, helping the Mavericks build the lead, and he put up 32 points in Dallas' season-opening loss to the Rockets . The NWSL introduced the rule late last year, allowing teams to spend an additional $1m above the salary cap to sign star players. Players with the designation had to meet one of eight criteria, ranging from US national team minutes and Ballon d’Or recognition to NWSL Best XI honors to media lists, including the Guardian’s Top 100 and a ranking that ordered athletes by marketability. item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. item.title: Is el clásico still the world’s biggest match? Three questions before Barcelona v Real Madrid
item.description: The fixture’s relevance waned as the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded. Can Lamine Yamal and Mbappé lift it into a new era? For the best part of a decade, el clásico was more than just soccer’s biggest fixture. It was the defining narrative. At the peak of the Lionel Messi v Cristiano Ronaldo era, there were clásicos everywhere. Yes, when the two historic rivals clashed on the pitch, but also in the voting for the Ballon d’Or every year and in so much of the discourse around the sport. As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico ’s relevance. This isn’t to say matches between Barcelona and Real Madrid no longer matter. They always have and always will. In 2026, however, it’s difficult to measure a clásico ’s standing. Is it still the sport’s biggest fixture? Continue reading...

item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. item.title: Bournemouth enjoy night to remember as 10-man Milan fail to weather storm
item.description: This was a momentous night in Bournemouth’s history, although the truth is they would have been given a far sterner examination by Coventry or Hull. Whatever this rotten impersonation of a Milan side was, it bore no relation to those that forged such a celebrated history. The visitors resembled holograms even before their goalkeeper Mike Maignan, with an extraordinary rush of blood resulting in a penalty and red card, rendered their task impossible. They never showed the slightest hint of putting up a fight. Bournemouth simply swamped the seven-time European champions and, amid a swirling south coast storm that rarely let up, could depart singing in the rain. Amine Adli’s sumptuous late free-kick, curled left-footed from 22 yards, meant they could finish the evening with the flourish they deserved. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Transfer window verdict: how every Premier League club fared
item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. Should Gabriel Martinelli complete his move to Al-Hilal as expected in the coming days – the Saudi Pro League window remains open – a few injuries could leave Arteta short. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game.
